entities.summary: Appian of Alexandria was a Greek historian with Roman citizenship who prospered during the reigns of the Roman Emperors Trajan, Hadrian, and Antoninus Pius. Born into a family of modest means, Appian's family was renowned for its literary and rhetorical talents, which he cultivated through extensive education and travel. He became a prominent historian and orator, producing works that showcased his mastery of Greek rhetoric and his deep understanding of Roman politics and society. Appian's most famous work, the 'Roman History,' provided a comprehensive account of the Roman Empire's rise to power, including the exploits of its most famous emperors. Through his writing, Appian played a significant role in shaping the Roman Empire's image and legacy, leaving a lasting impact on the development of Roman historiography. His works were widely studied and admired by scholars and leaders throughout the ancient world, cementing his reputation as one of the greatest historians of his time. Despite the passing of centuries, Appian's legacy continues to be felt in the fields of history, literature, and education.
